campaign.title: Architecture blocker resolution
constraints: No SPORE/ modification or inspection performed
No canonical SQLite knowledgegraph mutation performed
Static evidence was preferred; runtime plans are observations to run only if static evidence cannot decide

A.name: Noun/star publication lifecycle

resolved: Four physical root slots are distinct: DAT_0167eae0, DAT_0167eb60, DAT_0167eae4, and DAT_0167eb0c.
The noun path is receiver-compatible with cGameNounManager and materializes a noun-ID vector through a lower-bound map helper.
The star path is receiver-compatible with cStarManager and uses a lower-bound political-ID map plus an independently reference-managed current-player cache.
Noun object creation, list insertion, dirty-vector invalidation, object erase, and manager cleanup bodies are statically present.
Star empire map erase and current-player cache clearing are separate paths.
cStar is a live cGameData noun and cStarRecord is a separate serializable record linked through a typed pointer; physical aliasing is rejected.
unresolved: Root publishers, replacement, clear, and teardown stores
Value equality and phase identity for both root pairs
Whether the slots retain the same manager object, phase-specific objects, stale objects, or opaque service values
Exact root ownership and lifetime authority
Whether noun invalidation or star erase is always preceded by exact-key membership

strongest_evidence.finding: Each accessor reads a different global word; no direct root store or equality path was recovered.
Factory/list registration, lower-bound materialization, dirty-vector invalidation, staged destruction, and manager cleanup are direct.
Empire lookup is lower-bound, the current-player cache is lazy and reference-managed, map erase is separate from cache clearing, and stars.db replacement is a bounded database path.
Manager layouts and typed links support compatibility boundaries, not root publication ownership or logical identity cardinality.
No root serialization or runtime publication trace is available; SDK singleton language is corroboration only.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Each root pair always contains the same manager pointer.
predictions: Paired publication/clear stores
No unequal or null/stale window
Equivalent consumer behavior across accessors
contradictory_evidence: No paired direct writer or equality operation

competing_hypotheses.claim: Roots are phase-specific or independently rebound.
predictions: Unequal/null windows during initialization or transitions
Rebind order matters
Consumer behavior follows the selected root
supporting_evidence: Distinct words and independent manager families
Alternate star accessor is used by the player-empire cache path
contradictory_evidence: No runtime unequal window or root writer recovered

competing_hypotheses.claim: One accessor in each pair is stale or compatibility-only.
predictions: Consumers see old maps/lists after rebind
Canonical root teardown has no effect on active consumers
supporting_evidence: Alternate accessors have much larger fan-in
contradictory_evidence: Canonical star has a raw code reference
competing_hypotheses.status: unresolved; neither port may be removed

competing_hypotheses.claim: Publication occurs through computed, bulk, loader, or external paths.
predictions: Indirect store or data-table writer
Runtime write not visible as a direct literal xref
supporting_evidence: Slots are in a writable global service region
competing_hypotheses.status: possible but not selected as the leading explanation

adversarial_corrections: Four slots do not prove four owners, four lifetimes, or four publications.
Manager-compatible receivers do not prove that a root points to that manager.
Lower-bound invalidation and erase must be described as lower-bound-selected; exact-key membership is not proven.
A cStar noun and cStarRecord have distinct physical representations and a typed link; logical identity/cardinality remains unresolved.
The four-port boundary is safe only as a compatibility-excluded opaque observation seam with explicit host-side rebind/generation policy.
remaining_ambiguity: No proof of root unpublication order or final release
No complete star record-to-live-planet ownership trace
No exact-failure, locking, or callback cleanup contract
A.architecture_impact: A single-owner result could collapse the root graph; a phase-specific result forces phase-aware identities, rebind order, and separate teardown/cache graphs. The noun and star object graphs must remain physically distinct even if their logical records are associated.

exact_next_action.static_first: Trace constructor/registration results, aliases, bulk-copy helpers, tables, loader paths, and all computed writes/clears for the four root words.
exact_next_action.runtime_if_static_fails: One naturally reachable transition with synchronized captures of all four words, pointee addresses, vtable pointers, manager generations, noun/star map sizes, and teardown/release events. Include noun create/destroy, empire erase/cache refresh, and manager teardown.
exact_next_action.pass_condition: Produce a complete publisher/equality/teardown matrix; one unequal snapshot only rejects unconditional equality.

implementation_can_proceed_safely.boundary: Use four opaque observation ports with no implicit equality, fallback, owner claims, raw-pointer persistence, or original lifecycle emulation. Use lower-bound/successor-tolerant semantics only with explicit exactness postconditions where the replacement requires exact keys.

B.name: Forwarded state: DAT_0167eaec / 0x00b5b800

resolved: 0x00b5b800 reads DAT_0167eaec through 0x00b3d320, returns 0xffffffff for a zero receiver, and otherwise copies [receiver+0x20] through 0x00a42730.
The returned value is a borrowed 32-bit mode-domain scalar discriminator in observed consumers.
0x00b289ac and 0x00b5f056 are direct pointee-field writers for the current result of 0x00b3d320.
0x00b1d870 constructs a 0x9c cGameModeManager-compatible family and initializes +0x20 and +0x24 to -1, but is not statically joined to DAT_0167eaec.
unresolved: Whether DAT_0167eaec ever publishes the cGameModeManager-compatible allocation
Exact receiver class identity for the current pointee
First writer and first mode transition
Aliasing or pointer equality with canonical DAT_0167eb2c
Ownership, thread-safe lifetime, and whether the field is authoritative/current or a stale mirror

strongest_evidence.finding: The read path and -1 null path are exact and contain no ownership operation.
The current accessor result receives kLoadGameMode and normalized transition mode values.
A cGameModeManager-compatible object family has matching size, vtable, fields, allocation, and teardown, but no publication join to DAT_0167eaec.
The alternate global has one direct read and no recovered direct writer; the canonical global is a distinct slot with no demonstrated equality operation.
Mode-ID constants and transition payloads corroborate scalar mode semantics, but do not prove freshness or receiver identity.

competing_hypotheses.claim: A strategy/mode owner is forwarded through the slot.
predictions: Returned value is a mode ID
Mode transition writers and event consumers converge
competing_hypotheses.status: supported as semantic compatibility, not ownership proof

predictions: +0x20 changes on mode events
Value is scalar and copied by consumers
contradictions: No runtime trace or slot publication join

competing_hypotheses.claim: The returned value is a handle or pointer.
predictions: Returned value is dereferenced, virtually called, or retained as a pointer

competing_hypotheses.claim: The result is a tagged value.
predictions: A tag decoder or tagged-state representation is required
contradictions: Direct normalizer and mode constants explain the values without a tag layer
competing_hypotheses.status: not needed under the current model

competing_hypotheses.claim: +0x20 is a forwarded interface or strategy pointer.
predictions: +0x20 is dispatched or treated as a vtable/interface pointer
The earliest direct non-initializing mode store is the runtime first transition
evidence: It is an early direct mode writer
contradictions: Address order is not runtime order

adversarial_corrections: The cGameModeManager-compatible constructor is not proof that its allocation is published in DAT_0167eaec.
Pointee-field writers must not be reported as global-slot writers.
0xffffffff has at least two possible origins: zero receiver and -1 field state; the root does not distinguish them.
The safe API is a non-authoritative forwarded mode-word adapter, not an exposed cGameModeManager pointer or canonical active-state promise.
The alternate and canonical slots remain separate even if a runtime trace later observes equal values.
remaining_ambiguity: Runtime first writer and first mode transition
Slot publication, freshness, replacement, and teardown
B.architecture_impact: The existing mode-routing state machine can consume a scalar mode discriminator, but authoritative state ownership, publication lifecycle, and receiver typing remain open. A future pointer/tagged/strategy resolution would add an adapter and lifecycle model; it must not be smuggled into the current uint32 seam.

exact_next_action.static_first: Trace all aliases, bulk-copy paths, service registration, and computed writers for DAT_0167eaec and compare them with the cGameModeManager allocation at 0x00b1d870.
exact_next_action.runtime_if_static_fails: Record one allocation-to-slot-to-field chain: allocation base and vtable at 0x00b1d870, first non-zero alternate accessor result, canonical accessor result, [P+0x20] first write, and first replacement/clear/teardown.
exact_next_action.pass_condition: Establish P == allocation, P == canonical pointer or observed separation, and the first target field writer; otherwise retain the opaque adapter.

implementation_can_proceed_safely.boundary: Expose only a non-owning, non-authoritative mode-word adapter with explicit 0xffffffff handling and separate alternate/canonical freshness states. Do not expose the receiver, merge slots, claim first writer, or promise lifetime safety.

C.name: Persistence reference/restore and mode handoff

resolved: PropertyList has explicit local-entry Read/Write operations and typed-value dispatch, with an unresolved parent-related negative-count branch.
ClassSerializer uses ordered attribute descriptors and callback-based write/read dispatch with identity/count checks and status handling.
ISimulatorSerializable is a serialization capability, not proof of complete field coverage.
cSavedGameHeader and cCellSerializableData are serializer-vtable/copy-adopt candidates, not raw fixed blocks proven to be the whole save document.
Save/load candidates have static helper-local database/stream, header, service, and replacement sequences; stars.db replacement is separate.
App mode lifecycle, Simulator strategy state, and Cell runtime/presentation state are separate axes.
unresolved: Meaning of the shared 0x01A80D26 class/serializer identifier and descriptor key domain
Durable object-reference table, instance IDs, forward-reference/cycle behavior, and restore order
Property parent encoding and exact Property carrier layout
Whether cCellSerializableData is directly reached by the save/load candidates
Cell mode handoff/automatic save, cross-file atomicity, migration, field survival, and recovery

strongest_evidence.finding: Local property entries, parent branch, attribute setup, write/read callbacks, identity/count checks, and status checks are direct.
Runtime object association/create-or-reuse behavior exists, but durable persistence identity and cycle encoding are not established.
Header and Cell wrappers use serializer callbacks; Cell has a bounded in-memory DTO copy/adopt seam. Direct save/load participation is not fully joined.
Static operation sequences include path setup, database/stream lifecycle, header serializer calls, close, and temporary-path replacement; no universal transaction or crash atomicity is proven.
Mode exit/enter order and separate strategy state are direct; direct Cell OnExit/Dispose bodies do not call the observed save/load candidates, but higher-level autosave is not excluded.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Persistence uses a callback/class-attribute object graph with logical associations.
predictions: Class/attribute identity is checked before callbacks
References can be associated before field population
contradictions: Exact object table, durable instance IDs, and cycles unresolved

competing_hypotheses.claim: The header or Cell object is copied as a raw fixed struct.
predictions: Save/load would not require attribute callbacks or class/attribute validation
contradictions: ClassSerializer-backed header and Cell vtable methods

predictions: Save body directly writes a PropertyList or begins with it
DAT_0167eb34 or a manager vtable reaches 0x00b28ec0/0x00b279e0 as this
evidence: Persistence service accessor and SDK LoadGame surface
contradictions: Candidates call other service accessors; no manager this/vtable binding recovered

competing_hypotheses.claim: Cell OnExit/Dispose automatically saves or transfers a live graph.
predictions: Teardown reaches serializer/file helpers and preserves the live graph
evidence: Cell serializable object and copy/adopt helpers
contradictions: Live pool/presentation state is rebuilt separately
competing_hypotheses.status: no static autosave; higher-level behavior open

competing_hypotheses.claim: Temp/old/replace helpers establish one crash-atomic multi-artifact transaction.
predictions: A manifest/journal binds .spo and stars.db and rolls back failures
contradictions: Replacement paths are separate; no manifest or universal rollback recovered

competing_hypotheses.claim: Host addresses or Cell pool indices are durable object identity.
predictions: Save/load compares or serializes raw addresses
contradictions: Domain IDs, association helpers, refcounted owners, and DTO copy boundary
competing_hypotheses.status: rejected as a clean-room design; original exact behavior remains open

adversarial_corrections: The proposed object graph is a candidate clean-room architecture, not the smallest recovered original model.
Use SchemaKey/opaque descriptor identity until the shared 0x01A80D26 meaning and key scope are resolved.
Keep serializer/class keys, document instance handles, political/noun IDs, ResourceKeys, and Cell pool indices in separate domains.
Property parent state is an unresolved stream relationship with runtime resolution, not proven runtime-only data.
The save/load evidence is a static helper-local operation sequence, not a proven transaction or serialized-record order.
The Cell object remains a serializer/copy-adopt candidate until a direct save/load edge or runtime trace connects it.
Deferred binding, cycle detection, DTO handoff, staged replacement, and manifest/journal are OpenSpore policies, not recovered original guarantees.
remaining_ambiguity: Class/descriptor identity and durable object-reference encoding
Property value/parent encoding and round-trip behavior
Cell field survival and direct save/load participation
Persistence manager binding and restore order
Automatic mode save, cross-file atomicity, migration, and recovery
C.architecture_impact: The persistence seam must remain separate from live runtime ownership and from App mode lifecycle. OpenSpore may choose explicit schema, logical handles, deferred binding, DTO handoff, and staged artifact policies, but these are replacement contracts rather than recovered original compatibility. Raw pointers, Cell pool indices, and live GFX/UI handles remain prohibited from durable state.

static_first: Resolve the runtime-populated header and Cell descriptor tables and the read resolver key domain, including the shared 0x01A80D26 value.
Trace 0x00b28ec0/0x00b279e0 through Cell-specific helpers to 0x00e51300/0x00e51370 or prove the edge is absent.
Trace PropertyList constructor/getter/map-node layout and the negative-count parent branch.
Recover close/status branches before 0x006891f0 and the service vtable/this binding for the candidates.
runtime_if_static_fails: One explicit save/load round trip with a forward reference and, if naturally reachable, a cycle; record schema keys, callback order, object bindings, field whitelist, and failure behavior.
One Cell teardown without manual save, followed by explicit load/reopen; record serializer/file calls and whether copy/adopt helpers participate.
One controlled stream/callback failure and one successful two-artifact update to measure replacement and recovery.
exact_next_action.pass_condition: A candidate can be promoted to compatibility architecture only after descriptor identity, durable reference semantics, Cell save participation, field survival, and manager/transaction boundaries are separately observed.

implementation_can_proceed_safely.boundary: Use an OpenSpore-defined versioned document with explicit schema descriptors, typed property values, domain-separated logical handles, deterministic deferred binding, explicit DTO handoff, and independently specified artifact transaction/recovery policies. Do not claim original .spo/.prop bytes or runtime behavior.

synthesis.common_rule: No unresolved question may be promoted to a canonical type, singleton, owner, automatic save, exact lookup, raw-pointer identity, or cross-root teardown order.
synthesis.implementation_boundary: OpenSpore implementation may proceed only as a compatibility-excluded clean-room architecture using opaque/root observation seams and explicit domain contracts.
reopen_triggers: Original root/plugin ABI or manager identity is required
Original .spo/.prop/database bytes or field survival is required
Original Cell autosave, cross-mode live-pointer transfer, or restore order is required
Original multi-file atomicity, migration, or manager binding is required
